merger_description:
Airtree Ventures Opportunity Fund V Partnership, LP (**Airtree Fund**) proposes to acquire shares in Aegleon Holdco Pty Ltd (**Aegleon**) from Airtree Ventures Opportunity Fund V Trusco Pty Ltd as trustee of the Airtree Ventures Opportunity Fund V Stapled Trust.

As a result, Airtree Fund will indirectly acquire an interest in HotDoc Online Pty Ltd (**HotDoc**), a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Aegleon.

Airtree Fund is a venture capital fund managed by Airtree, which is a venture capital firm based in Australia which predominantly invests in early-stage and high-growth Australia and New Zealand-based technology companies. Funds managed by Airtree (including the Airtree Fund and the Existing Holder) hold minority investments in over a hundred companies in Australia, New Zealand and around the world.

Aegleon is a holding company incorporated in connection with the earlier acquisition of HotDoc by funds managed by Potentia, an Australian private equity firm specialising in technology and software investments.

HotDoc is a digital healthcare platform enabling patient engagement, scheduling, messaging, payments, and virtual care for general practitioners across Australia. HotDoc’s platform enables patients to book and manage their healthcare appointments with healthcare professionals.

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. Airtree will continue to have a small interest in HotDoc post-
Acquisition
b. there is no horizontal consolidation, removal of a competitor,
or change to Airtree’s competitive position as a result of the
Acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
The ACCC also considered the potential application of section
51ABD of the Act. The applicant submits that the Acquisition is in
substance an internal reorganisation, however, there is some
uncertainty about whether the Acquisition falls within the scope of
that provision due to the facts of this matter, including the nature of
the entities involved. Having regard to the particular circumstances,
including the consequences of non-notification in reliance on the
exemption if it was found not to apply, the ACCC considered it
appropriate to make a determination on the basis that the
acquisition provisions in the Act apply to the Acquisition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
